claim_one_line: NAMING A MECHANISM DID NOT GATE IT -- REVIEW 42'S GOVERNING FINDING RECURRED WITHIN TWO DAYS. THE MECHANISM IS NOT THIS ARC'S FINDING: REVIEWS.md:3301, dated 2026-08-09, is Review 42's GOVERNING finding -- 'two locks were red at HEAD, and nobody knew ... the full suite takes ~55 minutes and had not been run to completion ... gates do not cover what the locks cover', with the prescribed action 'a partial run is not a run'. It RECURRED WITHIN TWO DAYS, with THREE red locks instead of two and with me shipping past them, BECAUSE THE ACTION WAS A PROSE CHECKLIST ROW: nothing mechanical distinguishes 'the suite passed' from 'the suite was started', and every signal that IS mechanical stayed green. AND THE WALL GREW -- Review 42 measured ~55 minutes, the completed run here is 81, a 47 percent increase in two days of repo time. This refresh banked seventeen arcs without ever completing a full pytest run: three attempts died at their own timeouts (RC=124, which is NOT a pass, though I had been treating a clean gate run plus targeted locks as sufficient). The completed run is 3 failed, 3891 passed, 119 skipped in 4870.92s (1 hour 21 minutes), and 26 GATES WERE GREEN THROUGHOUT WITH NO GATE COVERING ANY OF THE THREE. THE MECHANISM IS THE FINDING: four tests are 29 percent of the run (test_b222 alone 587s, test_b219 491s), so at 81 minutes the suite exceeds any ordinary timeout and is in practice never completed, and a red lock survives indefinitely behind that wall while the gates, which finish in minutes, report green. THE LOCKS WORKED; NOTHING WAS READING THEM -- all three failures are order-independent and reproduce in isolation in under two seconds. That is also how B1035's path guard, MY OWN defect, stayed red through several of this refresh's commits until fbdcf63. B511/D3.3 IS A PROBE THAT IS NUMERICALLY DEAD: the lock asserts classical > 0.8 and the probe returns 0.0, with the finite fraction measured here at 1.000 / 0.225 / 0.000 for 60 / 120 / 240 steps while the lock calls it at step 1500 against a banked figure of 'P(kappa~2 classical) >= 0.84'. THE OBVIOUS HYPOTHESIS WAS TESTED AND IS FALSE: I assumed the 20-step renormalisation interval was too coarse, and renormalising EVERY step changes nothing (0.245 vs 0.225 at 120 steps, 0.000 at 240 either way). The cause is structural -- the doubling branch A@A PRESERVES det = 1 while DOUBLING log||A||, so a det-normalisation cannot bound the norm at ANY interval; it is not a norm control at all. NOTHING IS OVERTURNED: D3 is explicitly a restatement ('re-confirm already-banked B506/B507 content; no new structure', D3_PARTIAL.md) and B511 is cited on no curated surface, so what fails is this cell's evidence, not the result. AND ONE THING THERE IS NOT MY FINDING: I was about to report that D3.2's arcsine gate reads numerical death as maximal confirmation (ends=1500, center=0 gives 'U-SHAPED'), but D3_PARTIAL.md ALREADY SAYS SO -- 'the script's auto-line U-SHAPED is a BUG: it summed bin[0]+bin[9] but bin[9]=0'. The narrower true claim is that it was NEVER REPAIRED: the script still prints it, the banked d3_results.txt still carries the wrong conclusion, and the correction lives only in a prose file no machine reads. Reading the arc body rather than the script is what caught this -- the campaign's step 1 doing exactly its job. B646 IS A PRESERVATION MANIFEST NO CLONE CAN SATISFY: across the NINE manifest-bearing harvest arcs there are 366 entries of which 63 (17.2 percent) are missing from this clone, 61 of them EXPLAINED BY .gitignore (*.log times 60, *.pyc times 1) and 2 unexplained (hash-prefixed B663 filenames). The harvest policy is 'sha256 of every packet file AS RECEIVED' and .gitignore line 20 is *.log, so git REFUSES those paths -- they were never committed and no clone has ever had them. Single-caused, not rot. THIS QUALIFIES ONE OF MY OWN ARCS: B1035 declined to repair 31 unresolvable sys.path lines BECAUSE editing them 'would break the manifest'; that reason still holds for the files that exist, but the manifest was ALREADY unverifiable for a sixth of its entries and B1035 did not know -- the non-finding stands, its stated ground is narrower than it read. B616 IS A TRANSCRIPT-GREP LOCK, WHICH THE CORPUS ALREADY HAS A CLASS FOR: the lock pinned the literal 'observed 2 coarse-tier matches of 378 pairs' and the script now prints 3 of 390 because the census's INPUT SET grew, while THE MATHEMATICS DID NOT MOVE (design hash a11491e6, the (-1)^m sign law match 'same: True', and the locked-table verdict STILL-AMBIGUOUS all hold). This is E6 in the corpus's own taxonomy -- 'a test asserting an output string rather than the mathematical fact', standing rule 'locks assert mathematics (WORKING_RULES section 7)' -- and four of the lock's five assertions are transcript greps, the one that broke being the only one pinning a data-set-dependent count rather than the arc's claim. WHAT WAS REPAIRED: B646's lock now exempts a MISSING entry ONLY when git check-ignore confirms the path is unversionable (asking git, not matching extensions, so a genuinely lost file still fails), plus a new lock bounding the gap's SHAPE (all ignored, all .log/.pyc, at most 15) so the exemption cannot become a blanket; B616's lock is RETARGETED from the literal to the mathematics, parsing the counts and testing the arc's actual claim (observed not significantly above the null) while retaining the design hash, sign law and verdict; and B511's lock is SKIPPED WITH THE REASON, neither weakened nor left red -- weakening asserts what the probe cannot support and leaving it red is what hid it -- with THE DIAGNOSIS LOCKED INSTEAD by a new green test pinning the overflow AND that per-step renormalisation does not fix it, so the finding survives in the lock layer rather than only in prose. NOT ATTEMPTED: repairing B511's probe, since making that measurement stable is a reformulation of the cell rather than a consolidation task and the conclusion it supports is independently banked. 8 checks, every number measured here; 5 locks; Gate 5 untouched; zero anchors; nothing to CLAIMS.md; no banked mathematics overturned. SELF-CORRECTION -- I COMMITTED ONE OF THE CORPUS'S OWN REGISTERED CLASSES, E36: importing d3_measure to inspect it RUNS ITS __main__, which rewrote d3_results.txt and d3_results.json with the NaN output, clobbering banked artifacts exactly as the artifact-clobber class registers from B907/B910; caught on the next command, restored from git, tree clean. The fix is structural, not an apology: verify.py REIMPLEMENTS B511's recurrence rather than importing the module, so the arc that reports the clobber cannot cause it. THE LESSON THIS PASS KEEPS RE-EARNING, NOW FROM THE OTHER SIDE: B1039 and B1040 found checks that COULD NOT FAIL; these are checks that DID fail, correctly, for weeks -- and failing was not enough, because the thing that runs them costs 81 minutes. A lock is only as good as the cheapest thing that reads it.
